transcript:
Header: 2026-04-06 09:00 PT | Duration: 60 mins | Attendees: Ava, Diego, Leah, Samir, Nora, Owen, Priya, Tom, Jian, Marcos

Summary: quick Q2 launch readiness sync focused on runtime perf, KV cache telemetry, autoscaling safety, and incident learnings from last week's rollout. Action items and next steps captured.

[00:00] Ava Chen: Okay folks, thanks for joining. I know we have a packed agenda, I'm going to run through the launch readiness checklist then hand off to Diego for runtime perf updates.
[00:16] Diego Martinez: Cool, quick note, we had the partial rollout last Thursday — there were a couple of latency spikes around longer context lengths, looks like cache thrash when model fallback triggered.
[00:28] Leah Park: Yeah I dug in, and the KV cache invalidation was unusually high — around 14% miss rate for sessions over 2k tokens, might be the shard balancing plus bursty traffic.
[00:45] Tom Willis: Was that the same cluster that saw the 503s during the canary?
[00:51] Diego Martinez: Same pool, yes, though 503s were transient — some nodes hit memory pressure then OOMkilled a worker process. We recovered with the fallback policy but client saw retries.
[01:10] Priya Singh: From analytics, the affected customers were mostly high-context chat flows, and correlated with the model variant we had pinned. The revenue hit is small but it's a user visible regression.
[01:24] Samir Rao: Important to call out: rollout policy needs an additional safety net for long-context sequences — probably a per-route cap or earlier fallback rather than waiting for OOM.
[01:39] Diego Martinez: Agreed. On the kernel side, we're still seeing poor perf for 4k sequences on A100 with current quantized path — we suspect a vectorization mismatch. I'm coordinating with compilers team but it's midweek.
[01:58] Owen Kim: Also the orchestration layer didn't drain traffic quickly enough; pods were scheduled but not cordoned early. We need a pre-drain hook.
[02:11] Leah Park: I'll take pre-drain hooks for the autoscaler, but we should also add graceful cache warm-up so warmed pods advertise readiness only when KV warm rate > X.
[02:28] Diego Martinez: Good idea. We'll need a readiness probe that checks KV cache hit rate and KV prefetch status, otherwise we keep getting cold starts.
[02:40] Ava Chen: Let's keep this practical — main priorities: (1) make rollout safe for long contexts, (2) KV cache telemetry & dashboards, (3) autoscaler safety limits and pre-drain hooks, (4) final launch runbook.
[02:58] Marcos Alvarez: I'll update the runbook but need clear steps for rollback — like exact API toggle and rollback runbooks for both hosted and dedicated.
[03:10] Diego Martinez: For rollback, we have a model routing toggle in the control plane; I'll write the exact CLI command and add to the runbook.
[03:20] Nora Patel: QA found two flaky tests in the smoke suite that didn't catch the memory leak, I'll triage and add stronger memory assertions.
[03:31] Samir Rao: On the topic of cost vs latency, product wants to avoid downgrading model quality to hit latency SLAs. We should evaluate intelligent batching and KV tuning before swapping to smaller models.
[03:48] Priya Singh: Analytics shows batching gains are promising on steady-state traffic but adds tail latency on spikes. Might be worth adaptive batching.
[04:00] Diego Martinez: We can do adaptive batching with a max-latency cap; on burst detect we bypass batching. Implementation is non-trivial but doable.
[04:12] [04:12] (crosstalk) Leah Park: — and make sure fallback to smaller model variant is always logged with reason codes.
[04:20] Ava Chen: Good. Diego, Diego, can you give a quick status on kernel/compiler work and ETA?
[04:28] Diego Martinez: Briefly: compiler team found a vectorization pattern mismatch in the attention kernel for certain seq len shapes. They have a patch, testing now. If green, we can roll in two days, otherwise we need to gate. ETA 48-72 hours.
[04:45] Priya Singh: If that patch is delayed, what's our mitigation?
[04:49] Diego Martinez: Mitigations: quantization tweak to a different code path that trades 3-5% quality for 15-20% perf; or route long contexts to larger GPU nodes in Dedicated-like pool which is costlier.
[05:05] Samir Rao: Product prefers the kernel fix path; cost option only if needed. But we must be transparent in the runbook about tradeoffs.
[05:15] Jian Li: From infra angle, routing long-context to a different pool is feasible but we need capacity reservations. That means commit in Dedicated or reserved infra which impacts cost forecast.
[05:28] Ava Chen: Noted. OK let's move to telemetry: Leah, what's the minimum dashboard we need for launch?
[05:36] Leah Park: KV cache hit-rate per model and per route, memory usage per pod, per-node OOM counts, concurrency per pod, and end-to-end 95th latency broken by seq len buckets. Also alerts if KV hit drops below 85% or OOM rate > 0.5 per hour.
[05:56] Nora Patel: Add smoke test pass rate and canary failure rate.
[06:02] Leah Park: Yep. I'll set those up and send dashboard links.
[06:07] Marcos Alvarez: Can you add a short blurb I'll paste into the runbook about how to interpret the KV hit graph — e.g., cold start warm-up expectation and thresholds.
[06:18] Leah Park: Sure.
[06:20] [06:20] (background: keyboard sounds)
[06:25] Ava Chen: Incident retro quick: last week, primary driver was unexpected memory churn in the runtime under long context workloads; root cause appears to be a combination of a garbage collection surge in the runtime and the kernel inefficiency. We treated symptoms with scaling and fallback but need to fix root cause.
[06:46] Diego Martinez: I'm putting together a postmortem; early notes: reproducible with synthetic long-context load generator, reproduces across two instance types. We should include microbenchmarks in the PM.
[06:58] Priya Singh: Analytics helped isolate affected customers and impacted endpoints; I'll attach the chart.
[07:05] Ava Chen: Great. Let's capture who owns the postmortem and the actionables.
[07:12] Diego Martinez: I'll own the postmortem draft, with Leah and Owen contributing infra and SRE sections. Nora will add QA validation steps.
[07:22] Samir Rao: One more ask from product: make sure the launch plan includes stakeholder comms — a short status page item and customer-facing notice if we expect any performance variances.
[07:33] Marcos Alvarez: I'll draft the customer note but need PR review.
[07:38] Ava Chen: Alright, any blockers?
[07:41] Owen Kim: We need more capacity headroom on the reserve pool for long context routing if we choose that path; procurement needs numbers by EOD Friday for an emergency reserve.
[07:51] Priya Singh: I can provide usage projections by tomorrow.
[07:55] Diego Martinez: Also need approval for the compiler team to do the kernel patch roll — low risk but requires release window.
[08:03] Ava Chen: We'll coordinate with release ops, Samir will own the release window coordination.
[08:10] Samir Rao: Got it.
[08:12] [08:12] (brief silence)
[08:15] Ava Chen: Recap — Diego finalizes rollout CLI and postmortem draft; Leah creates dashboards and readiness probes; Diego & Leah implement pre-drain hook and readiness warm-up; Nora fixes flaky smoke tests; Marcos publishes runbook and customer note; Owen + Priya coordinate capacity numbers. All due next week, most by 2026-04-09 to 2026-04-13.
[08:44] Nora Patel: I'll start triage immediately and post updates in the shared doc.
[08:49] Diego Martinez: I'll publish the canary rollback CLI snippet into the runbook after this call.
[08:55] Marcos Alvarez: I'll aim to publish the runbook draft by tomorrow EOD.
[08:59] Ava Chen: Excellent. Any last comments?
[09:02] Tom Willis: One ask — can we add a small traffic generator in staging that mimics multi-turn 4k sessions? Would help catch this earlier.
[09:11] Diego Martinez: We have a basic one; I'll extend it to multi-turn and share.
[09:16] Ava Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene Tues if needed.

Notes: transcription contains some mis-heard tokens (e.g., "OOMkilled" appears as "oom kill" in parts of the raw export), and speaker labels may be simplified. Links referenced in call: /docs/launch-runbook (draft), /dashboards/kv-cache, internal spreadsheet: https://redwood-internal.example.com/sheets/launch-capacity

End of transcript.
